Binary search, step by step

Binary search finds a value in a sorted array by looking at the middle and throwing away the half that cannot hold it. Each step halves the range.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Search the whole array: lo is the first index, hi the last.
  2. Look at the middle index, mid.
  3. If the value at mid is the target, stop.
  4. If it is smaller, search right of mid. If larger, search left of mid.
  5. When lo passes hi, the target is not in the array.

Cost

Time
O(log n). Best case O(1) when the middle is the target.
Space
O(1) for this loop version.
Needs
A sorted array.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain binary search with stepthru tracer calls, such as range and pointer, that record each step.
